newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Zinc barely changed in featureless Asian trade.
newsitem.headline: Zinc barely changed in featureless Asian trade.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) zinc prices were barely changed in featureless Asian trade on Thursday after hitting a fresh 4-1/2 year peak, traders said.
Zinc hit the high on Wednesday at US$1,311 a tonne before pulling back. It closed late on Wednesday at $1,303 a tonne.
"We expect some retracement in zinc prices today as profit-taking (is) expected," a trader with Tong Yang Futures said.
The trader said three-month zinc would probably head higher after completing its current consolidation.
He pegged short-term resistance for zinc at $1,315-$1,330 a tonne and did not rule out the possibility of the metal surging to $1,400 a tonne in the medium term.
But another futures broker said zinc would need more time to breach the upper end of the range because the oversold situation in the market would pare buying interest.
The 14-day relative strength index (RSI) for three-month zinc was standing at 67.59, compared 70.62 percent a day before and 66.74 percent a week ago.
The market generally considers an RSI of 70 or more as overbought and 30 or less as oversold.
"If three-month copper price breaches (the) upper end of the current range, zinc will easily break the resistance," he said.
Three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange (LME) was seen remaining consolidating in a range of $2,350-$2,380 a tonne before setting a new direction, traders said.

Copper's fundamentals are backed by good interest in Singapore warrants along with brisk demand in the Far East against a background of some production problems in the U.S. which would limit any downward move in the market, they said.

They said Wednesday's option declaration passed quietly as several major options granters were believed to have completed switching their nearby positions to far forward months before the Easter holidays.
